cards.definitions: G(n,1/2) is the distribution on simple labeled graphs with vertex set {1,…,n}, with each unordered pair independently made an edge with probability 1/2. A proper q-coloring assigns each vertex one label in {1,…,q}, with adjacent vertices receiving different labels. Use real variables x_{v,c} as color indicators and equations x_{v,c}²−x_{v,c}=0, x_{u,c}x_{v,c}=0 for every edge {u,v}, and Σ_c x_{v,c}−1=0. The 2021 strong formulation also explicitly includes x_{v,c}x_{v,c′}=0 for c≠c′. For a specified set of polynomial equations h=0 and integer D≥2, its degree-D pseudoexpectation is a linear map L from real polynomials of total degree at most D to ℝ with L(1)=1, L(p²)≥0 whenever 2 deg p≤D, and L(ph)=0 for every equation and multiplier with deg(ph)≤D. Feasibility means such an L exists, so this relaxation cannot refute colorability. The weak formulation instead uses Σ_c x_{v,c}≥1 and its SoS inequality conditions, allowing multiple colors at a vertex in the underlying Boolean constraints. Probability statements are over G and high probability means probability tending to one as n→∞. D counts polynomial degree, not running-time exponent or the number of variables.
cards.answer_criterion: A completed residual formulation must specify the precise axiom presentation, the allowed D and q regimes, the success probability and the requested asymptotic precision, then seek matching feasibility and refutation bounds at that precision. Merely proving a higher-degree lower bound at q=n^{1/2+ε} is already covered by the 2025 result and cannot count as resolving a new open question.

cards.title: Does random-start tensor power iteration eventually recover a component?
cards.formal: For a fourth-order tensor T=Σ_{i=1}^k aᵢ^{⊗4} with independent aᵢ∼N(0,I_d/d), does tensor power iteration from an independent random direction recover one of the component directions, up to sign, within polynomially many iterations throughout the overcomplete regime d≪k≪d²? The source conjectures positive recovery despite its polynomial lower bound on convergence time, but does not quantify the required recovery error or all dependencies of the polynomial bound.
cards.why: Would distinguish a long initial transient from a genuine algorithmic failure in a basic nonconvex tensor method, under a standard random overcomplete model.
cards.status_note: The original model, recurrence, rank convention and lower-bound theorem were read and compared with the June 2024 JMLR result. Author research listings and subsequent-result searches through 12 September 2026 did not yield a resolution of this overcomplete-model question. Its requested quantitative recovery guarantee remains informal.

cards.definitions: The input consists of the entries of the symmetric real tensor T∈(ℝᵈ)^{⊗4}; the individual aᵢ are hidden. Each aᵢ has independent coordinates of mean zero and variance 1/d, and all components are mutually independent. Let x₀ be uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius √d and independent of these components. Define zₜ=T(I,xₜ₋₁,xₜ₋₁,xₜ₋₁)=Σᵢ⟨aᵢ,xₜ₋₁⟩³aᵢ and xₜ=√d·zₜ/‖zₜ‖₂. On the null event of a zero denominator, declare the run failed. No new tensor samples or independent noise are introduced between iterations. The same dynamics is normalized gradient ascent for S(x)=Σᵢ⟨aᵢ,x⟩⁴. The regime means integer sequences k=k(d) with k/d→∞ and k/d²→0 as d→∞; it is not restricted to k=d^c for a fixed exponent c. Directional error can be measured by min_{i,s∈{−1,+1}}‖xₜ/√d−s aᵢ/‖aᵢ‖₂‖₂, but the source does not specify its required size. Probability is over both the tensor components and the independent initial direction. The paper studies iteration counts with exact real arithmetic, not bit complexity of Gaussian input encodings. The target is recovery of one component; recovery of the entire decomposition is a different task.
cards.answer_criterion: A precise completion must give a recovery tolerance, success guarantee, stopping/output rule and the permitted parameter dependence of a polynomial iteration bound, then prove or refute that bound for the stated random model. A theorem that only shows the objective increasing, assumes an initially correlated component, or analyzes a planted single-spike tensor with Gaussian noise does not settle the source question.

context_blocks.title: Overcomplete means more components than dimensions
context_blocks.text: The tensor combines k hidden directions in ℝᵈ with k much larger than d. Randomness is imposed on the entire collection of directions, rather than on additive observation noise.

context_blocks.title: Random initialization can lead to a long delay
context_blocks.text: For d^{3/2}≪k≪d², Theorem 3.1 proves that all iterates up to T=o(k^{2/3}/(d(log k)^{1/3})) have vanishing normalized correlation with every component. For fixed k comparable to d^c with 3/2<c<2, this entails a polynomial delay.

context_blocks.title: A polynomial delay does not rule out polynomial recovery
context_blocks.text: The authors’ numerical evidence motivates eventual polynomial-time success. Their lower bound disproves an overly rapid convergence expectation, not that later polynomially many iterations can work.

context_blocks.title: The later tensor PCA theorem concerns different randomness
context_blocks.text: The 2024 paper gives a sharp positive analysis for one planted spike plus a tensor of independent Gaussian noise entries. That is not the overcomplete sum in this question, even though both use randomly initialized power iteration.

context_blocks.title: What still needs specification
context_blocks.text: The informal positive conjecture says “correctly learn” in polynomial time but does not prescribe the recovery error, its dependence on d and k, or a uniform polynomial iteration bound across all sequences d≪k≪d². A precise stopping/output convention is also needed if success means a returned iterate rather than visiting a good iterate. The normalized iteration and rank regime are recoverable, but an exact numerical error target or a polynomial-in-accuracy claim must not be invented.

cards.title: Are algebraic branching programs stronger than formulas?
cards.formal: For a fixed field F, is VF_F a proper subclass of VBP_F? Equivalently, is there a family (fₙ) of polynomials of polynomially bounded degree in polynomially many commuting variables that has polynomial-size algebraic branching programs over F but no polynomial-size algebraic formulas over F? The field is a parameter of the question, as in the source; a result must state the fields to which it applies.
cards.why: Separates two fundamental models of algebraic computation and asks whether sharing path computations gives a polynomial-versus-superpolynomial advantage over arithmetic trees.
cards.status_note: Recovered the exact containment from the source and checked subsequent work through 12 September 2026, including the January 2026 multilinear paper. No unrestricted resolution was located. The May revision notice for ECCC TR26-043 reports a gap in that separate barrier claim, which is not used as an established result here.

cards.definitions: A polynomial family has fₙ∈F[x₁,…,x_{m(n)}], where m(n) and the total degree of fₙ are at most n^a+a for some fixed a. An algebraic formula is a finite rooted tree whose leaves are variables or constants in F and whose internal gates are binary addition or multiplication. Its output is a formal polynomial; equality means coefficientwise equality in F[x], also when F is finite. Its size is its number of nodes. An algebraic branching program is a finite directed acyclic graph with a designated source and sink and affine-linear polynomial labels on edges. It computes the sum, over all source-to-sink paths, of the product of the labels on that path. Count vertices, edges and the nonzero coefficients used to describe edge labels as its size; these choices differ only polynomially from the usual size conventions. Field constants have unit algebraic cost, with no bit-length bound. VF_F and VBP_F consist respectively of the polynomial families with formula size and branching-program size bounded by n^b+b for some constant b independent of n. These are nonuniform classes: a different finite computation may be chosen for each n, with no requirement to generate it algorithmically. The separation asks for one family in VBP_F for which, for every b, some n requires formula size greater than n^b+b. There is no restriction to multilinear computation, bounded depth, homogeneous intermediate gates or noncommuting variables.
cards.answer_criterion: For the stated field F, prove VF_F ⊊ VBP_F by exhibiting a family in VBP_F and proving that its formula sizes are not polynomially bounded, or prove VF_F=VBP_F by showing that every polynomial-size branching-program family has polynomial-size formulas. Any characteristic or field restriction must be stated as part of the scope of the answer. A lower bound only for bounded-depth or multilinear formulas does not resolve the unrestricted question.

cards.title: A dimension-free directed L¹ Poincaré inequality
cards.formal: Does there exist an absolute constant C<∞ such that, for every integer n≥1 and every Lipschitz function f:[0,1]ⁿ→ℝ, d₁^mono(f) ≤ C ∫_[0,1]ⁿ (Σ_{i=1}^n max{−∂ᵢf(x),0}²)^{1/2} dx? Here d₁^mono(f) is the L¹ distance to the coordinatewise nondecreasing functions. The same C must work for every dimension and every finite Lipschitz constant.
cards.why: Would connect local directional decreases to global distance from monotonicity with a universal constant, extending a central isoperimetric principle to real-valued functions on continuous cubes.
cards.status_note: The full 2023 conjecture, October 2024 preprint revision and July 2025 thesis were checked, including the explicit statement that the later norm inequality does not resolve this one. Searches through 12 September 2026 located no resolution of the full continuous-cube claim.

The multiplicative constant must be independent of the dimension and the Lipschitz constant.
A known inequality using the sum of coordinate decreases loses a square-root dimension factor.
Later work proves a different inequality using squared quantities and explicitly leaves this conjecture open.

references.title: Directed Poincaré Inequalities and L¹ Monotonicity Testing of Lipschitz Functions

cards.definitions: Lebesgue measure on [0,1]ⁿ has total mass one. A function g:[0,1]ⁿ→ℝ is coordinatewise nondecreasing if g(x)≤g(y) whenever xᵢ≤yᵢ for all i. Define d₁^mono(f)=inf_g ∫|f(x)−g(x)|dx, over measurable integrable coordinatewise nondecreasing g; g need not have the same Lipschitz constant as f. A function f is Lipschitz if there is a finite L with |f(x)−f(y)|≤L‖x−y‖₂ for all x,y in the cube. Its gradient exists almost everywhere; its values on the exceptional null set may be set to zero without changing any integral. The negative gradient is ∇⁻f(x)=(max{−∂₁f(x),0},…,max{−∂ₙf(x),0}). The right-hand side is C·E[‖∇⁻f(X)‖₂] for a uniform point X in the cube. It is not C·(E[‖∇⁻f(X)‖₂²])^{1/2}. No boundary condition, mean-zero assumption or fixed bound on the range of f is imposed.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the displayed inequality with one universal finite C, or refute the existence of such a C by showing that the ratio d₁^mono(f)/E‖∇⁻f‖₂ is unbounded across the stated functions and dimensions (including a function with positive distance and zero denominator, if one existed). A bound whose constant grows with n, or a bound using the L² norm of the gradient over the cube, is insufficient.

context_blocks.title: A local violation versus a global repair
context_blocks.text: A negative partial derivative witnesses a local decrease in one coordinate. The left-hand side measures the least average change to the entire function needed to remove all monotonicity violations.

context_blocks.title: The dimension-free Euclidean norm is the missing improvement
context_blocks.text: The 2023 source proves a directed inequality using E‖∇⁻f‖₁. Comparing ℓ₁ and ℓ₂ norms yields a bound with a factor √n, whereas the conjecture asks to remove all dependence on dimension.

context_blocks.title: The 2024 theorem uses a different outer norm
context_blocks.text: The later theorem bounds squared L² distance to monotonicity by C·E‖∇⁻f‖₂². Even though L² distance dominates L¹ distance, the square root of this second moment can be much larger than E‖∇⁻f‖₂. The author explicitly leaves the present conjecture open.

context_blocks.title: The conjecture survived the improved tester
context_blocks.text: The 2025 thesis restates the inequality after obtaining a tester with sublinear dimension dependence from the L² theorem. Thus the motivating algorithmic progress and the analytic conjecture have distinct statuses.

cards.context:
A negative partial derivative witnesses a local decrease in one coordinate. The left-hand side measures the least average change to the entire function needed to remove all monotonicity violations.

The 2023 source proves a directed inequality using E‖∇⁻f‖₁. Comparing ℓ₁ and ℓ₂ norms yields a bound with a factor √n, whereas the conjecture asks to remove all dependence on dimension.

The later theorem bounds squared L² distance to monotonicity by C·E‖∇⁻f‖₂². Even though L² distance dominates L¹ distance, the square root of this second moment can be much larger than E‖∇⁻f‖₂. The author explicitly leaves the present conjecture open.

The 2025 thesis restates the inequality after obtaining a tester with sublinear dimension dependence from the L² theorem. Thus the motivating algorithmic progress and the analytic conjecture have distinct statuses.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Individual editorial review of saved titles, importance rationales, problem statements, source notes and working summaries. This is a review of importance and topical diversity, not a fresh verification of open status or completion of draft formulations. Importance scores are preserved.
